description.narrative: JustificationMost poor households in Kenya do not have health and life insurance cover and most insurance industry companies struggle with too high work-flow costs to profitably serve the bottom of the pyramid with health and life insurance.What holds these insurance industry companies back from widespread servicing of the low-income segment, is a lack of digitization and data.SummaryThe intervention supported DDFinance to scale up and refine existing operations and reach in Kenya. The intervention supported DDFinance’s efforts in improving the company’s digital Insurance Platform as a Service (IPaaS) to handle new B2B business streams, enabled smooth integrations with underwriting partners and enhanced user experience. The funding supported marketing activities that increased number of households covered with micro-insurance and supported expansion activities in Kenya and Burundi. At the end of the intervention 59.129 persons had received health and life insurance, The assumption for the intervention was that DDFinance had built IPaaS as a digital infrastructure to support a digital marketplace for Life and Health insurance, capable of allowing Kenyan incumbents to benefit from the technological infrastructure that reduces work-flow costs through effective digital distribution channels and allowing access to un- or underserved low-income mass markets.Based on these assumptions DDFinance aimed to scale the operations in Kenya and expand into Burundi and Zambia. DDFinance succeeded to expand in Kenya and Burundi but not yet to Zambia and further across the continent. The recent good success from contracting with four microfinance banks for their distribution of health and life micro-insurance on IPaaS, as an embedded part of their microloan distribution, provides a challenging but possible venue for the intervention / DDFinance to enable 100 million people to be covered with health and life micro-insurance by year 7 from intervention start.
